stem: Given log(x) + log(y) = log(12) and log(x) - log(y) = log(3), find the value of x. (All logarithms are to base 10.)

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student solves for y instead of x: xy=12 and x/y=3 give x=6, y=2. If student uses y = sqrt(12/3) = sqrt(4) = 2 and calls it x, they get 4.
log(xy) = log(12) gives xy = 12; log(x/y) = log(3) gives x/y = 3. Multiplying: x^2 = 36, so x = 6.

Student reads log(x) - log(y) = log(3) as log(x/y) = log(3) correctly, but then sets x = 12/y = 12/4 = 3 by using a wrong value of y=4 from an earlier arithmetic slip. Or student solves x = 12 - 3 = 9 treating log arguments as additive.
Student solves x/y = 3 only (ignores the sum equation) and takes x = 3 directly without using xy = 12 to pin down the individual value of x.

explanation: Using log laws: log(x) + log(y) = log(xy) = log(12) gives xy = 12. log(x) - log(y) = log(x/y) = log(3) gives x/y = 3. Multiplying the two equations: x^2 = 36, so x = 6 (taking positive root since x must be positive for log to be defined).

explanation_sections.punchline: Convert log equations to algebraic equations xy=12 and x/y=3, then multiply to get x^2=36, so x=6.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply log product and quotient laws to strip the logs: log(x)+log(y)=log(xy) and log(x)-log(y)=log(x/y). Set xy=12 and x/y=3. Multiply these two equations to eliminate y: x*x = 12*3 = 36, so x = 6.
explanation_sections.lesson: Two log equations can be converted to two algebraic equations; multiply them to eliminate the unknown variable cleanly.
explanation_sections.timing: 75-90 seconds. The trap is solving y first from x/y=3 with y=12/x substitution, which is longer. Direct multiplication of xy and x/y is the fastest path.
